newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks drop sharply after Dow pull-back.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks drop sharply after Dow pull-back.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.915 -0.075 Gold NY 339.35 Lon fix 338.00
AUD US$0.7523 (Mon $0.7513) CRB Index cl 241.25 +0.73
*Stocks opened lower after the Dow fell 192 points or about 2.5 percent on Monday. Total volume 57.5 million, value A$118.3 million, 748 stocks traded, 230 steady, 68 up, 450 down.
Australian shares opened weaker across the board on Tuesday, the market reacting predictably to a sharp pull-back of the Dow industrials index on Monday.
At 10.25 a.m. (0025 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 24.7 points lower at 2681.6.
The June share price index was 27 points down at 2692 and at a 10.4 point premium to the underlying index.

Early selling was spread equally between industrial and resource issues. Nearly all blue chip stocks opened weaker and falls were being led by bellwether companys, the Broken Hill Pty Co and National Australia Bank.
"Building materials and property stocks are holding up fairly well but not so the banks," said Scott Healey, a dealer at Brisbane broker, Wilson HTM.
Healey said banks were suffering the effects of rate rise fears after the Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto made comments which triggered a wave of profit-taking on Wall Street.

"People would have been very nervous this morning but a 192 point fall on Wall Street really isn't very much in the scheme of things," said Michael Heffernan, head of research at Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Heffernan said he expected to hold up reasonably well for the remainder of the session.
"I think institutions were looking for a bit of a pull-back so they could top up thier holdings," he said.
Fund managers have a vested interest in supporting the market at its current levels until the end of the Australian financial year on June 30 as portfolios are valued for the year at this date.
One of the most active stocks early was newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings which recently has been subject of takeover speculation.
